rounds.text: Coforge demonstrates extraordinary fundamental momentum, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 42% [E17] and a staggering net profit growth of 92% over the same period [E21]. This exceptional operational performance is underpinned by elite returns on capital, with a robust ROCE of 23.5% [E12] and a 5-year median return on equity of 22% [E27], both significantly outperforming sector medians. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally cash-generative, achieving a cash conversion ratio of 1.03x in March 2026 where operating cash flows reached Rs 1,792 Cr alongside Rs 1,197 Cr in free cash flow [E34, E35, E36]. Market confidence is strongly validated by a rules-based screen score of 90 out of 100 carrying a high-confidence BUY rating [E64], driven by powerful year-over-year sales surges of 54% [E65] and net profit increases of 42% [E67]. Technical strength mirrors these fundamentals perfectly, as the stock commands a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 while trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49, E50]. Conceded: [E44] a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value below the current market price resulting in a negative margin of safety.

Coforge Ltd trades at a steep price-to-earnings ratio of 41.8x, far exceeding the sector benchmark P/E of 41.36x against 19.58x, and sits near the very top of its 52-week range [E1, E5, E6]. This premium valuation is unsupported by intrinsic value models, as a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 1929 per share against a market price of Rs 2045, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -6.0% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the company's borrowings have escalated dramatically to Rs 6,026 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 728 Cr a year earlier, alongside negative flags indicating that the tax rate seems low and interest costs might be capitalizing [E39, E62, E63]. Institutional backing has also eroded significantly, with foreign institutional holding dropping from 34.04% to 24.75% and domestic institutional holding falling from 55.02% to 43.79% since Dec 2023 [E41, E42]. Conceded: [E62], [E63]. While the bear highlights a negative DCF margin of safety at -6.0% [E45], this model ignores the phenomenal fundamental momentum where TTM sales growth hit 42% [E17] and TTM profit growth reached an astonishing 92% [E21]. The valuation multiple of 41.8x [E1] is fully justified by elite capital efficiency, including a robust 23.5% ROCE and 21.4% ROE [E12, E13] that vastly outperform sector medians [E10, E9]. The dramatic escalation in borrowings [E39] is offset by exceptional cash generation, with operating cash flow at Rs 1,792 Cr and free cash flow at Rs 1,197 Cr, meaning profits are fully backed by cash at 1.03x conversion [E34, E35, E36]. Conceded: [E41], [E42]. Despite institutional holding shifts, total money flow reads POSITIVE with an increase in overall institutional holdings [E43], and the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 90 out of 100 [E64] backed by a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50].

Conceded: [E12], [E13], [E34], [E35], [E36], [E43]. While the bull points to elite ROCE and strong cash flow, it glosses over the fundamental valuation disconnect where the discounted cash flow model explicitly places intrinsic value at Rs 1,929 against a market price of Rs 2,045, leaving a negative margin of safety of -6.0% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current price already demands an aggressive 18.8% earnings growth, while official screening signals flag that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E46, E69]. The bull's dismissal of balance sheet strain ignores that borrowings surged to Rs 6,026 Cr in September 2026 from just Rs 728 Cr a year prior [E39], alongside company flags warning that the tax rate seems low and interest cost might be capitalized [E62, E63]. Finally, reliance on relative strength and momentum ignores historical vulnerability, given a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -88.5% and institutional outflows reflected by foreign and domestic holdings dropping significantly since late 2023 [E41, E42, E52].

Conceded: [E44, E45, E46]. While the DCF models point to a slight negative margin of safety and a high growth expectation, the underlying fundamentals comprehensively dwarf the bear's warnings, led by an elite 23.5% ROCE and a 21.4% ROE that vastly outperform sector medians [E12, E13, E75]. The bear's alarm over borrowing increases ignores the company's powerful cash generation, boasting Rs 1,792 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 1,197 Cr in free cash flow with a fully backed 1.03x cash conversion rate [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, institutional capital is responding to this structural strength rather than fleeing, as reflected by a positive money flow signal and an institutional holding change of +1.61 percentage points alongside an absolute relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E43, E50]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence 90 out of 100 BUY score driven by staggering 54% YoY sales growth and 42% YoY net profit growth [E64, E65, E67].

Conceded: [E12, E13]. While the high ROCE and ROE are present, the bull dismisses the valuation disconnect highlighted by the discounted cash flow model showing a negative -6.0% margin of safety and a share price of Rs 2,045 sitting above the Rs 1,929 intrinsic value [E44, E45]. The reverse DCF proves that today's price already demands an aggressive 18.8% earnings growth rate, which leaves zero room for error especially when screens explicitly warn that earnings growth is decelerating [E46, E69]. Furthermore, while operating cash flows appear strong at Rs 1,792 Cr, total borrowings have dramatically surged to Rs 6,026 Cr in Sep 2026 up from just Rs 728 Cr a year prior, alongside troubling red flags that the company may be capitalizing interest costs and reporting a low tax rate [E35, E39, E62, E63]. The bull's reliance on institutional money flow ignores the broader multi-year exodus where foreign institutional holdings dropped from 34.04% to 24.75% and domestic institutional holdings fell from 55.02% to 43.79% since December 2023 [E41, E42, E43]. Finally, chasing this strength at 94% to 98% of the 52-week range carries severe tail-risk given the historical max drawdown of -88.5% and a high annualized volatility of 42.5% [E5, E47, E52, E53].
